'''Jared Malcolm Xavier Sullinger'''<ref>{{cite web |title=Jared Malcolm Xavier Sullinger () - Basketball Stats, Height, Age |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/players/240623-jared-malcolm-xavier-sullinger |website=FIBA Basketball |access-date=3 January 2025}}</ref> (born March 4, 1992) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He is currently the director of player development for the [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State Buckeyes.]] He played [[college basketball]] for Ohio State before being selected 21st overall by the [[Boston Celtics]] in the [[2012 NBA draft]].

==High school career==
Sullinger was rated as the #2 player in the class of 2010 in the [[ESPNU]] 100,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/rankings|title=College Basketball Recruiting - ESPNU 100 - ESPN|publisher=[[ESPN]]|access-date=August 26, 2010}}</ref> the #4 player by [[Scout.com]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=9&c=4&pid=88&yr=2010|title=Scout.com: Football Recruiting|publisher=Scouthoops.scout.com|access-date=August 8, 2010}}</ref> and the #5 player by [[Rivals.com]].<ref name="rivals">{{cite web|url=http://rivalshoops.rivals.com/viewrank.asp?ra_key=1909|title=Yahoo Sports: Rivals.com Ranking - Rivals150 for class of 2010|publisher=Rivalshoops.rivals.com|access-date=August 26, 2010}}</ref> In his senior year, Sullinger led Northland High School to a 21–0 season and a #1 national ranking. He averaged 24.5 points and 11.7 rebounds for the season.<ref name="dispatch1">{{cite web|url=http://www.dispatch.com/live/content/sports/stories/2010/03/10/naismith-awards.html|title=Northland High School basketball player, father win national Naismith awards|publisher=The Columbus Dispatch|date=March 10, 2010|access-date=2010-08-26|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100314065158/http://www.dispatch.com/live/content/sports/stories/2010/03/10/naismith-awards.html|archive-date=March 14, 2010}}</ref> Sullinger played in the 4th annual [[Boost Mobile]] Elite 24 Hoops Classic.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.slamonline.com/online/college-hs/college/2009/08/boost-mobile-elite-24-roster-announced|title=Boost Mobile Elite 24 Roster Announced|publisher=Slam Online|date=August 5, 2009|access-date=August 26, 2010|archive-date=July 4, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100704010316/http://www.slamonline.com/online/college-hs/college/2009/08/boost-mobile-elite-24-roster-announced/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Sullinger was selected to play in the [[2010 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2010 McDonald's All-American Game]] in [[Columbus, Ohio]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.slamonline.com/online/college-hs/high-school/2010/02/mcdonalds-all-american-game-team-announced|title=McDonald's All-American Game Team Announced|publisher=Slam Online|date=February 11, 2010|access-date=August 26, 2010}}</ref> where he was named co-MVP with [[Harrison Barnes]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.maxpreps.com/news/m2xSkj0QEd-lugAcxJTdpg/mcdonalds-all-american-night--knights-3-pointer-wins-it-for-the-west.htm|title=McDonald's All-American night: Knight's 3-pointer wins it for the West - MaxPreps News|publisher=Maxpreps.com|date=March 31, 2010|access-date=August 26, 2010}}</ref> He was also selected to play in the 2010 [[Nike Hoop Summit]] at the [[Rose Garden (arena)|Rose Garden]] in [[Portland, Oregon]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.slamonline.com/online/college-hs/high-school/2010/01/its-the-usa-against-everyone-else|title=It's the USA Against Everyone Else|publisher=Slam Online|date=January 20, 2010|access-date=August 26, 2010}}</ref> and the 2010 [[Jordan Brand Classic]] at [[Madison Square Garden]] in [[New York City|New York]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.slamonline.com/online/college-hs/high-school/2010/02/jordan-brand-all-american-game-team-announced|title=Jordan Brand All-American Game Team Announced|publisher=Slam Online|date=February 18, 2010|access-date=August 26, 2010}}</ref>

On March 10, 2010, Sullinger won the [[Naismith Prep Player of the Year Award|James A. Naismith Award]], which goes to the boys' high school basketball player of the year.<ref name="dispatch1"/>

Sullinger committed to Ohio State on May 10, 2007.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.escoutroom.com/eScoutRoom/Articles/ArticlesDetail/tabid/702/smid/1331/ArticleID/898/Default.aspx|title=A Summer Full of Events for #1 Center in the Country, Jared Sullinger|publisher=Escoutroom.com|date=May 5, 2007|access-date=August 26, 2010}}</ref>

==College career==
===Freshman===
[[File:Jared Sullinger Ohio State.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Sullinger at Ohio State]]
Sullinger had 19 points and 14 rebounds in his Ohio State debut.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20101117002952/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=303160194 Ohio State routs North Carolina A&T in season opener]</ref>
Sullinger's brother, J.J. Sullinger, also attended Ohio State and played for coach [[Thad Matta]]. For the 2010–11 season Jared Sullinger averaged 17.2 points, 10.2 rebounds and 1.2 assists in 31.7 minutes per game for the Buckeyes. Leading the Buckeyes to a [[2011 Big Ten men's basketball tournament]] championship, being named [[Big Ten tournament Most Outstanding Player|MOP]]. Ohio State finished the regular season at 32–2 and was selected as the [[2011 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2011 NCAA tournament]]'s number one overall seed. The Buckeyes made it to the "Sweet Sixteen" where they lost to [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] 62–60. Sullinger was named a First Team All-American by [[Fox Sports (United States)|Fox Sports]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Jeff|last=Goodman|url=http://msn.foxsports.com/collegebasketball/story/duke-blue-devils-notre-dame-fighting-irish-represented-postseason-honors-030711|title=Goodman's 2010-11 All-America teams|work=[[Fox Sports (United States)|Fox Sports]]|publisher=Fox Sports Interactive Media|date=March 7, 2011|access-date=June 21, 2011}}</ref>

===Sophomore===
In what would be his final year at Ohio State, Sullinger led the Buckeyes to a 31–8 overall record (13–5 Big Ten). He averaged 17.5 points and 9.3 rebounds per game during the 2011–12 season. The Buckeyes advanced to the 'Final Four' of the [[2012 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2012 NCAA tournament]], where the team lost to the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas Jayhawks]]. Sullinger had 13 points in the game and was 5-of-19 shooting with 11 rebounds in the loss. Five days after the loss, the two-time [[Associated Press|AP]] All-American declared he was entering the 2012 draft, where he was widely expected to be a lottery pick, until he was reportedly flagged by several teams after the Chicago pre-draft camp due to back issues.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2012/story/_/id/8069495 Jared Sullinger's back a concern]</ref>

==Professional career==
===Boston Celtics (2012–2016)===
====2012–13 season====
[[File:Jared Sullinger dunk.jpg|thumb|Sullinger going up for a dunk with Boston]]
On June 29, 2012, Sullinger was selected with the 21st overall pick in the [[2012 NBA draft]] by the [[Boston Celtics]]. On July 3, he signed his rookie scale contract with the Celtics.<ref name="SullingerSigns">{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press_release/press070312-celtics-sign-2012-draft-picks.html|title=Celtics Sign 2012 NBA Draft Picks|work=NBA.com|date=July 3, 2012|access-date=December 9, 2014}}</ref> On November 17, he recorded his first [[double-double]] with 12 points and 11 rebounds in a 107–89 win over the [[Toronto Raptors]]. The following night, he scored a season-high 16 points in a loss to the [[Detroit Pistons]]. He tied that mark on December 25, recording 16 points and 7 rebounds in a 93–76 win over the [[Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/s/sullija01/gamelog/2013/ Jared Sullinger 2012-13 Game Log]</ref>

On February 1, 2013, Sullinger underwent successful lumbar disk surgery and was subsequently ruled out for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2013/news/02/01/jared-sullinger-injury.ap|title=Celtics' Sullinger out for season with back injury|work=NBA.com|date=February 1, 2013|access-date=August 21, 2013}}</ref>

====2013–14 season====
On January 15, 2014, in a win over the Toronto Raptors, Sullinger recorded 25 points and a career-high 20 rebounds. Sullinger's 20-20 was the first by a Celtics player since [[Kevin Garnett]] did so in 2007.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400489442|title=Celtics top Raptors 88-83, end 9-game skid|access-date=January 15, 2014|date=January 15, 2014|work=ESPN.com}}</ref> On February 7, he scored a career-high 31 points in a 99–89 win over the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/games/20140207/SACBOS/gameinfo.html Notebook: Celtics 99, Kings 89]</ref>

====2014–15 season====
After averaging 14.4 points and 8.1 rebounds per game up until the [[2015 NBA All-Star Game|2015 NBA All-Star Weekend]], Sullinger was ruled out indefinitely after X-rays on February 19 revealed a stress reaction in his left foot.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/boston/nba/story/_/id/12349920 Jared Sullinger out indefinitely]</ref> Three days later, he was ruled out for the rest of the season after further medical evaluation determined that Sullinger had sustained a left metatarsal [[stress fracture]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/jared-sullinger-injury-update-0 Jared Sullinger Injury Update]</ref> However, in a surprising move, Sullinger returned to action on April 3 against the Milwaukee Bucks. He entered the game four minutes into the third quarter, missed both his shots and didn't return as part of a gradual effort to improve his stamina.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/games/20150403/MILBOS/gameinfo.html Ilyasova leads 3rd-quarter surge, Bucks top Celtics 110-101]</ref>

====2015–16 season====
Sullinger began the 2015–16 season coming off the bench for the first three games. He started his first game of the season on November 4 against the [[Indiana Pacers]], replacing [[Tyler Zeller]] as the starting center.<ref>[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/s/sullija01/gamelog/2016/ Jared Sullinger 2015-16 Game Log]</ref> On December 7, 2015, Sullinger scored 11 points and tied a career high with 20 rebounds in a 111–93 win over the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151207/BOSNOP/gameinfo.html |title=Thomas leads Celtics past struggling Pelicans 111-93 |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2016-01-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160111001639/http://www.nba.com/games/20151207/BOSNOP/gameinfo.html |archive-date=2016-01-11 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>[http://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/celtics-jared-sullinger-ties-career-high-20-boards/ Celtics' Jared Sullinger: Ties career-high 20 boards]</ref> On February 7, 2016, he tied his season high with 21 points in a 128–119 win over the Sacramento Kings.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160207/SACBOS/gameinfo.html |title=Avery Bradley's 25 points helps Celtics beat Kings |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2016-02-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160208081641/http://www.nba.com/games/20160207/SACBOS/gameinfo.html |archive-date=2016-02-08 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On June 29, 2016, the Celtics tendered a qualifying offer to make Sullinger a restricted free agent. The Celtics later withdrew their qualifying offer on July 8, making him an unrestricted free agent.<ref>[http://fansided.com/2016/07/10/boston-celtics-letting-jared-sullinger-leave/ Boston Celtics letting Jared Sullinger leave]</ref>

===Toronto Raptors (2016–2017)===
On July 14, 2016, Sullinger signed a one-year, $6 million contract with the [[Toronto Raptors]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/raptors/press-releases/sullinger-071416|title=Raptors Sign Jared Sullinger|work=NBA.com|date=July 14, 2016|access-date=July 14, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Mazzeo|first=Mike|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/16989742|title=Jared Sullinger agrees to deal with Toronto Raptors|work=ESPN.com|date=July 11, 2016|access-date=September 19, 2022}}</ref> On October 24, 2016, he had a screw inserted into the fifth metatarsal in his left foot.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/raptors/press-releases/sullinger-surgery|title=Jared Sullinger To Undergo Foot Surgery|work=NBA.com|date=October 23, 2016|access-date=January 19, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Rowan|first=Justin|url=http://hoopshabit.com/2016/10/26/toronto-raptors-jared-sullinger-injury|title=Jared Sullinger's Injury Could Be A Big Problem For The Toronto Raptors|work=HoopsHabit.com|date=October 26, 2016|access-date=January 19, 2017}}</ref> As a result, he missed the first half of the 2016–17 season. After missing half the season, Sullinger made his debut for the Raptors on January 18, 2017, scoring eight points in just under 14 minutes off the bench in a 94–89 loss to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Ganter|first=Mike|url=https://nationalpost.com/sports/basketball/nba/jared-sullinger-makes-debut-for-toronto-raptors-in-94-89-loss-to-philadelphia-76ers|title=Jared Sullinger makes debut for Toronto Raptors in 94-89 loss to Philadelphia 76ers|work=NationalPost.com|date=January 19, 2017|access-date=January 19, 2017}}</ref> On January 28, 2017, he was assigned to Toronto's [[D-League]] affiliate, [[Raptors 905]], on a rehab assignment.<ref>{{cite assignment|work=SportsNet.ca|date=January 28, 2017|access-date=February 6, 2017}}</ref> He was recalled by Toronto the next day.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/raptors-jared-sullinger-recalled-from-d-league|title=Raptors' Jared Sullinger: Recalled from D-League|work=CBSSports.com|date=January 29, web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=400899391|title=Raptors vs. Celtics – Box Score|work=ESPN.com|date=February 1, 2017|access-date=February 3, 2017}}</ref> He was reassigned to Raptors 905 on February 10,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/raptors-jared-sullinger-assigned-to-d-league|title=Raptors' Jared Sullinger: Assigned to On February 23, 2017, Sullinger was traded, along with cash considerations and Toronto's second-round draft picks in 2017 and 2018, to the [[Phoenix Suns]] in exchange for [[P. J. Tucker]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/phoenix-suns-trade-pj-tucker-toronto|title=Phoenix Suns Trade P.J. Tucker to Toronto|work=NBA.com|date=February 23, 2017|access-date=February 23, 2017}}</ref> However, he was waived by the Suns the following day.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-sign-price-waive-scott-sullinger|title=Suns Sign Price, Waive Scott, Sullinger|work=NBA.com|date=February 24, 2017|access-date=February 24, 2017}}</ref>

===Shenzhen Leopards (2017–2018)===
On September 12, 2017, Sullinger signed a one-year deal with the [[Shenzhen Leopards]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Jared Sullinger inks in China with Shenzhen Leopards|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/asia/china/246615/jared-sullinger-inks-in-china-with-shenzhen-leopards.html|access-date=September 25, 2017|work=Sportando.com|date=September 25, 2017}}</ref> He re-signed with the team on August 6, 2018.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jared Sullinger re-signs with Shenzhen Leopards |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/asia/china/284822/jared-sullinger-re-signs-with-shenzhen-leopards.html |publisher=Sportando |access-date=August 6, 2018 |date=August 6, 2018 }}{{Dead link|date=October 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref> On January 16, 2018, Sullinger became one of the few players in the CBA to record 40 points and 30 rebounds in a single game as he posted 40 points and 31 rebounds in a 129–103 victory over the [[Shandong Golden Stars]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/international/boxscores/2018-01-16-shenzhen.html|title=CBA China - Shandong Golden Stars at Shenzhen Leopards, Jan 16, 2018|date=January 16, 2018|publisher=Basketball Reference|accessdate=June 15, 2021}}</ref>

=== Anyang KGC (2021) ===
In February 2021, Sullinger joined [[Anyang KGC]] of the Korean league and helped the team capture the league championship.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Murphy |first1=Patrick |title=Jared Sullinger helps Anyang KGC to KBL title, takes home Finals MVP award |url=https://247sports.com/college/ohio-state/Article/Ohio-State-basketball-Jared-Sullinger-helps-Anyang-KGC-to-Korean-Basketball-League-title-takes-home-Finals-MVP-award-165239087/ |access-date=December 28, 2021 |work=247 Sports |date=May 10, 2021}}</ref> He averaged 27.1 points, 12.3 rebounds, 3.2 assists, and 1.4 steals per game.<ref name="obradovic"/>

===Return to the Leopards (2021–2024)===
On December 26, 2021, Sullinger returned to the Shenzhen Leopards of the Chinese Basketball Association (CBA).<ref name="obradovic">{{cite web |last1=Obradovic |first1=Igor |title=Sullinger is back at Aviators, ex Anyang KGC |url=https://www.asia-basket.com/China/news/723597/Sullinger-is-back-at-Aviators,-ex-Anyang-KGC |website=Asiabasket |access-date=December 28, 2021 |date=December 26, 2021}}</ref> In April 2024, Sullinger was named CBA International Most Valuable Player for that season after averaging 21.8 points, 11.3 rebounds, and 4 assists per game.<ref name="CD24">{{cite news |title=Xinjiang forward Abdusalam wins CBA MVP award |url=https://www.chinadailyhk.com/hk/article/580364 |access-date=6 March 2025 |work=China Daily|date=8 April 2024}}</ref>

===Beijing Royal Fighters (2024-2025)===
In December 2024, Sullinger made his debut with the [[Beijing Royal Fighters]] of the Chinese Basketball Association.

=== Guangdong Southern Tigers (2025-2026) ===
On November 16, 2025, Jared signed with [[Guangdong Southern Tigers]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sina Visitor System |url=https://passport.weibo.com/visitor/visitor?entry=miniblog&a=enter&url=https%3A%2F%2Fweibo.com%2F2012390301%2F5233684061098740&domain=weibo.com&ua=Mozilla%2F5.0%20%28Macintosh%3B%20Intel%20Mac%20OS%20X%2010_15_7%29%20AppleWebKit%2F537.36%20%28KHTML%2C%20like%20Gecko%29%20Chrome%2F110.0.0.0%20Safari%2F537.36%20Citoid%2FWMF%20%28mailto%3Anoc%40wikimedia.org%29&_rand=1763301579642&sudaref= |access-date=2025-11-16 |website=passport.weibo.com}}</ref>

===Retirement===

On September 3, 2026, Sullinger announced his retirement from professional basketball to take up the position of Director of Player Development as part of the [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State Buckeyes men's  basketball team]] under head coach [[Jake Diebler]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jared Sullinger Joins Diebler’s Staff as Director of Player Development |url=https://ohiostatebuckeyes.com/news/2026/9/3/mens-basketball-jared-sullinger-joins-dieblers-staff-as-director-of-player-development |access-date=2026-09-04 |website=Ohio State |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
On September 3, 2013, Sullinger turned himself in to police after an alleged domestic assault on his girlfriend. He was charged with assault and battery, intimidation of a witness, and destruction of property. He pleaded not guilty to the charges,<ref>{{cite web | last=King | first=Jay | url=http://www.masslive.com/celtics/index.ssf/2013/09/jared_sullinger_arrested_bosto.html | title=Jared Sullinger arrested: Boston Celtics forward turned himself in after domestic incident, according to report | work=masslive.com | date=September 3, 2013 | access-date=September 3, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/2013/news/09/03/celtics-sullinger-arrested.ap/ | title=Celtics' Sullinger pleads not guilty to domestic assault | work=NBA.com | publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. | date=September 3, 2013 | access-date=September 3, 2013}}</ref> which were later dropped.<ref>{{cite web | last1=Abel | first1=David | last2=Ellement | first2=John R. | title=Charges dropped against Celtics' Sullinger | website=BostonGlobe.com | date=2013-10-28 | url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/2013/10/28/domestic-violence-charges-against-boston-celtics-player-jared-sullinger-dismissed-woman-refused-testify-against-him/kbTYfd71u1ygi4jd4S0ONK/story.html | access-date=2025-12-12}}</ref>
